facts.statement: Ofcom Spring 2026 update was published on 13 May 2026.
The report is a snapshot of UK mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability as of January 2026.
The comparison baseline Connected Nations 2025 used July 2025 data.
Fixed broadband reporting covers fixed-line and fixed-wireless-access networks.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises.
Full-fibre availability represented 82% of UK homes.
The residential premise base used was 30.5 million homes.
Full-fibre availability increased by 1.2 million homes in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up increased by 1.8 million connections in the same six-month period.
Full-fibre take-up reached 12.4 million connections across residential and commercial premises.
Full-fibre take-up represented 47% of premises with access to full fibre.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 89% of UK homes.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 27.1 million homes.
The prior July 2025 gigabit-capable availability rate was 87%.
The prior July 2025 gigabit-capable availability count was 26.4 million homes.
Premises without access to affordable decent broadband fell to about 4,000.
Premises unable to access decent broadband by fixed line or fixed wireless fell to 39,000.
The corresponding July 2025 fixed/fixed-wireless not-decent count was 44,000.
Good 4G geographic coverage from all MNOs reached 84% of UK landmass.
Good 4G geographic coverage from at least one MNO remained at 96% of UK landmass.
Each MNO maintained predicted 4G coverage outside at least 99% of UK premises.
5G Standalone coverage outside premises ranged from 49% to 85% across deployed MNOs.
The July 2025 5G Standalone comparison range was 47% to 65%.
Overall 5G coverage outside premises ranged from 76% to 94% by MNO.
